answer: The relic multiplier is published, charged in vertex, and walnut lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3905 identities would post 3610 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
